thread:
Alex Nguyen: FYI customer SkyMail reporting intermittent 429s for the last ~90m on their production traffic. They say it started around 18:05 UTC. Endpoint mainly /v1/chat -> model redwood-rlhf-13b. They see lots of quick retries that worsen the burst. Can someone check attribution (route vs model vs org quota)?

Zoe Park: pinging the logs now. do we have the org_id?

Alex Nguyen: org_id org-456. I have a sample request they sent (sanitized):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -d '{"model":"redwood-rlhf-13b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"summary"}]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
```
They included response headers, example: `x-rw-limit: 120/s`, `x-rw-remaining: 0`, `x-rw-reset: 12` and body with 429.

obs-bot: ALERT: 429-rate-spike detected in prod-east - window 18:04-18:12 UTC. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/observability/alerts/429-spike-1949980500 :rotating_light:

Mike Chen: we pushed a runtime tweak to batching/autoslice at 17:58 UTC in prod-east (small change to max-batch-size for some chat routes). Could be interacting with per-route burst limiter. Ill check model variant labels.

Asha Patel: quick repro check: ask customer to run `curl -v` so we capture response headers. If `x-rw-remaining` cycles to 0 before the spike, that's quota. If remaining >0 and they still get 429, it's the rate limiter at the route boundary.

Zoe Park: pulled logs -> quick query I used (internal logs / Insights):
```sql
-- count 429s by route, model, and org in last 1h
select route, model_name, org_id, count(*) as n429
from api_events
where status_code = 429 and timestamp >= now() - interval '1 hour'
group by route, model_name, org_id
order by n429 desc
```
Results (top rows):
- route: /v1/chat, model: redwood-rlhf-13b, org: org-456, n429: 1208
- route: /v1/chat, model: redwood-13b-quant, org: org-789, n429: 56
- route: /v1/embeddings, model: rw-embed-2, org: org-456, n429: 3

Zoe Park: summary: 99% of the 429s for the time window are on /v1/chat for org-456 and map to redwood-rlhf-13b. Looks route-scoped not org-global quota.

Alex Nguyen: so it's not billing/auth. good. can we see limiter logs (reservation failures)?

Mike Chen: yes. here's a quick projection query we run on the limiter metrics (Prometheus style):
```promql
sum(increase(api_rate_limiter_denied_total{route="/v1/chat"}[1h])) by (route, model_name, customer_id)
```
I ran it for the window and got: route=/v1/chat model=redwood-rlhf-13b customer=org-456 -> 1170 denies. That lines up with Zoe's event counts.

Zoe Park: also cross-checked the kernel/exec change: at 17:58 we adjusted max-batch-size from 16 -> 32 for a subset of chat shards. That increases instantaneous concurrency per worker and can cause more reservation failures under steady capacity.

Jordan (oncall): did autoscaling kick?

deploy-bot: AUTOSCALE: pool chat-prod-east scaled up by 2 nodes at 18:06 UTC due to CPU pressure, policy: scale-by-usage.

Mike Chen: autoscale happened but theres a short gap between the bursts and actual new capacity. Batching change increases token throughput per request, so latency briefly rises and more concurrent reservations get rejected until new nodes come up. Classic burst-overrun.

Asha Patel: recommended customer-facing phrasing: "We observed transient per-route rate limiting for your /v1/chat traffic while runtime adjustments triggered higher instantaneous concurrency. This led to HTTP 429s; we've tuned autoscaling and the runtime and it should stabilize. Please retry with exponential backoff and jitter. If issues persist we will pin a lower batch profile for your org."

Alex Nguyen: any dashboard/alert improvements to prevent blindspots?

Zoe Park: yes — create a composite alert that fires on both: 1) spike in `api_responses{code="429"}` AND 2) increase in `rate_limiter_denied_total` grouped by `route, model_name` with a short window (5m). Current alert only groups by region which hides per-route flares.

Mike Chen: add a heatmap panel in Observability Console: x-axis time, y-axis model_name+route, value = 429 count / minute, with per-org filter. also add a pre-aggregation for `429_ratio = increase(429[5m]) / increase(requests_total[5m])` so we alert on ratio > 1%.

Zoe Park: runbook snippet to add to alert: steps -> link logs (ql), run limiter query, check autoscale / pool status, check recent runtime deploys, escalate to eng-runtime if limiter denies > 500 in 10m.

Asha Patel: small repro command to share to customer to validate headers: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-rlhf-13b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat` and paste `x-rw-*` headers back here.

Mike Chen: mitigation we pushed: rollback the experimental batch-size increment on the hot shards and staggered autoscale warmup. I just merged a canary fallback policy that will fallback to a smaller model variant automatically when limiter denies exceed threshold.

Zoe Park: closing notes: cause = per-route burst/reservation failures triggered by batching change + autoscale lag. attribution -> route=/v1/chat, model=redwood-rlhf-13b, customer/org-456. Not auth/billing.

Alex Nguyen: thanks all. action items: (1) Asha: send SkyMail a short postmortem + suggested backoff header handling, (2) Mike: confirm canary fallback is enabled and document, (3) Zoe/Jordan: create/update composite alert + add heatmap panel. I'll update ticket and notify customer. :thumbsup:

Jordan (oncall): @mike @zoe please loop me in the pager if this spikes again.

Mike Chen: will do.

obs-bot: RESOLVED: 429-rate-spike (prod-east) - incident closed 18:20 UTC.

Alex Nguyen: sending status to customer now.
